newsitem.title: USA: Judge allows developer to join Ill. COPs lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Judge allows developer to join Ill. COPs lawsuit.

text.p: A Cook County, Ill., judge Friday allowed the developer of a downtown Chicago office building to become a defendant in a lawsuit challenging the legality of $19.2 million of certificates of participation issue.

Judge Michael Getty ruled that National Build to Suit Clinton L.L.C., the building's developer, "clearly has a claim of interest" in the case. He granted a motion by the Illinois Department of Central Management Services to allow the developer to join the department as a defendant in the case.
Edmund Moran, a Chicago attorney representing a group of Democrat lawmakers from the Illinois House that filed the lawsuit in June, had argued that the lawsuit was directed solely at state officials.

But attorneys representing central management services, which entered into a lease-purchase agreement with the developer for the building on behalf of the Illinois Department of Public Aid, contended that the developer was a necessary and indispensible party to the lawsuit. The lease-purchase agreement resulted in the issuance of $19.2 million of COPs last February.
The lawmakers' suit charged that the COPs constitute state debt and as such central management services exceeded its constitutional and statutory authority in issuing or causing to issue the COPs.

Moran said he expected the defendants to use Getty's ruling allowing the developer in the suit to seek a change of judges. In July, Getty gave the lawsuit the green light by ruling there were reasonable grounds for it to proceed.
Brad Kapnick, an attorney at Sidley & Austin, who is representing central management services, said he did not know what the developer would do.
